summary: I confirmed and fixed all 8 findings in crates/search-store, each with a regression test. While testing with many random seeds of the model test I found two more data-loss bugs. Both came from my first fix for finding 1, and both are now fixed and have their own regression tests. clippy, rustdoc and every test are green, and the model test passed 200 extra random seeds for each of its three variants. No new dependencies; root Cargo.toml and pg-storage were not touched.
public_api:
use search_store::*; everything from earlier rounds stays the same except the changes below.
CHANGED behaviour:
- read_manifest, read_latest_manifests, recover_shard(s), read_cluster and branch read exactly the newest generation. An object-store error or a damaged object is now an Err that names the key ("reading shard manifest <key>", "shard manifest <key> is damaged", "reading cluster state <key>", "cluster state <key> is damaged"). They never fall back to an older generation.
- delete_shard with manifest_retain_ms > 0 writes a tombstone generation (`<version>.deleted.json`) instead of deleting the commit points. The shard is then gone for read_manifest, read_manifests, list_shards, read_latest_manifests, recover_shards and branch-from-now, but a branch to a time before the deletion restores it. collect_garbage removes the shard's history once the tombstone is older than the window. With a window of 0, the commit points are deleted at once, as before.
- After delete_shard, any write of that shard on this node (write_manifest, attach_shard, a flush racing DELETE) fails with "shard [uuid][n] of cluster [c] was deleted". This lasts until release_cluster. A tombstone also refuses such writes from every node.
- Manifest and cluster-state keys use 20-digit epoch and generation fields: `<epoch:020>-<gen:020>-<token:016x>`. Any u64 epoch now works. A generation overflow is an error.
- Each WAL run writes a marker `search/wal/<node>/<first file:016>.run` at Wal::open. A node's numbering always starts past every earlier run's marker.
NEW:
- `WalSource::exact: bool`. It is set when another node froze the range from a listing. At replay, any non-skipped file missing from an exact range fails with "WAL files … of node [n] are missing … acknowledged operations would be lost".
- `GcStats::manifests_deleted`, `GcStats::run_markers_deleted`.
- `keys::{run_key, parse_run_key, tombstone_key, shard_version_key, parse_shard_version, ShardVersion, TOMBSTONE_SUFFIX}`. `ShardVersion` is also re-exported at the crate root.
- `keys::ClusterObject::Manifest` gained a `deleted: bool` field.
done: 1 (major, confirmed): a shard left attached by a crash kept every later WAL object of its node referenced. Fix: Wal::open writes a run marker (`search/wal/<node>/<first file>.run`) before any append. An open range now ends one file before the next run's marker: GC applies this in src/gc/mod.rs and freeze() in src/wal/replay.rs, so recovering such a shard reads only its own run's files. GC deletes markers that no open range needs, but always keeps each node's newest. Regression test: tests/wal.rs a_crashed_run_does_not_pin_the_nodes_later_wal (the reviewer's reproduction: only the crashed run's files survive GC, and the shard still replays elsewhere).

Follow-on bug from fix 1, found with ROLL_MODEL_RUNS (an acknowledged operation was lost): after GC deleted all of a node's WAL objects, a restart numbered its files from 1 again, below an older run marker. That marker then ended the new run's own range early. Fix: first_file = max(remote, local, newest marker) + 1. Regression test: tests/wal.rs runs_start_past_every_earlier_run_even_after_their_files_are_collected, which I checked fails without the fix.

Second follow-on bug from fix 1, found with the point-in-time model: branch_point merged consecutive ranges that spanned a node restart into one range. Freezing that merged range at its first run's end dropped the later run's operations. Fix: branch_point freezes each range before merging (src/branch.rs). merge_sources also combines `exact` with a logical AND. Regression test: tests/store.rs point_in_time_branches_span_a_restart_of_the_writing_node, which I checked fails without the fix.

2 (major, confirmed): reads now take exactly the newest generation. I/O and decode errors propagate with the key named. If the newest object is gone (only a concurrent delete does that), the read lists again, up to 3 times. Regression tests: tests/store.rs unreadable_latest_generations_are_errors_not_older_ones (chmod 000 on local objects: read_manifest, recover_shard, read_latest_manifests, recover_shards, read_cluster and branch all fail, then succeed once readable; a damaged state also errors). The damaged-manifest assertions in manifests_are_generational_with_retention_and_fallback and waking_a_cluster_reads_every_shard_at_once now expect errors.

3 (major, confirmed): inside the point-in-time window, delete_shard writes a tombstone generation. branch_point treats a tombstone at or before the requested time as 'deleted', and GC expires a tombstoned shard's history once the tombstone leaves the window. Regression test: tests/store.rs a_point_in_time_branch_restores_a_deleted_index (the reviewer's reproduction: the restore gets index A's segment and its unflushed operation; branches from now or after the deletion have no shard; GC keeps the history inside the window and deletes it, then the segment, outside the window).

4 (minor, confirmed): ranges frozen from another node's listing are marked `exact`, and replay fails on a missing non-skipped file instead of leaving a gap. Ranges closed without a listing can have legitimate gaps after a crash, so they stay lenient. Regression test: tests/wal.rs a_lost_wal_object_in_a_frozen_range_fails_replay (the reviewer's reproduction).

5 (minor, confirmed): ShardTrack has a `deleted` flag. delete_shard keeps the track until release_cluster, and put_manifest refuses writes when the flag is set or the newest generation is a tombstone. Regression test: tests/store.rs a_flush_after_delete_does_not_bring_the_shard_back.

6 (minor, confirmed): Version keys use 20-digit fields, so any u64 epoch works, and generation overflow returns an error. Regression tests: tests/store.rs epochs_of_any_size_are_readable (epochs 7, 10^16 and u64::MAX, plus fencing) and the extended keys::tests (16-digit and over-u64 keys are rejected; key order holds at every magnitude).

7 (minor, confirmed): upload_segment hands the cache the canonical id.file_name(). Regression test: tests/store.rs uppercase_segment_file_names_are_cached_under_the_canonical_name (1 hit, 0 misses, 1 file).

8 (minor, confirmed): in Cache::fetch the verified map now lives until place() and is passed in as the existing map, so the file is mapped only once. Regression test: cache::tests::a_verified_download_is_mapped_once (the map the verifier checked is the same Arc the cache returns, for both a small and a multi-part download).
Tests that list WAL objects now use a common::wal_files helper that skips run markers.

Docs: module docs in keys.rs, manifest.rs, gc/mod.rs and wal/replay.rs, and the search-store section of docs/search/contracts.md (strict reads, tombstones, run markers, exact ranges, the 20-digit key format, and the marker and tombstone rows in the key table).
remaining: Run the suite against S3 (SeaweedFS with ROLL_E2E_S3_BUCKET) again; it was not re-run this round. The new objects (markers and tombstones) are plain PUTs and nothing relies on listing order, so a difference is unlikely. The unreadable-object test always uses local storage.

Known ambiguity, existing before this round: if a crashed run opened a range at a file number it never wrote, and the next run starts at that same number, the range is treated as the new run's own. It stays open and over-retains files (it never loses data) until the next restart. Fixing it needs a run id inside WalSource.

search-server (not this crate): handle the new strict-read errors. A damaged newest manifest or state now fails the shard or cluster open instead of opening an older one; an operator deletes the damaged key. Treat 'was deleted' errors from a flush that raced DELETE /index as expected.

Carried over: search-index integration of SegmentFetch, and search-server wiring (Verifier, StoreProvider over read_cluster/write_cluster, recover_shards on wake, flushes chosen with pinning_shards, WalFull answered with 429).
tests: All green. cargo clippy -p search-store --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean. RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p search-store --no-deps: clean. cargo test -p search-store: 74 pass; 2 benchmarks and 1 doctest are ignored. That is 28 unit tests, 25 in tests/store.rs (6 new), 18 in tests/wal.rs (3 new) and 3 in tests/model.rs. With ROLL_MODEL_RUNS=200, all three model variants pass 200 extra random seeds each (about 170 s). Before the two follow-on fixes, random seeds failed with lost acknowledged operations. The S3 (SeaweedFS) run was not repeated.
notes_for_others: search-server: a damaged or unreadable newest manifest or cluster state is now an error naming the key, never a silent older generation. Surface it as a failed shard or cluster rather than retrying blindly.

search-server: delete_shard is safe to call while a background flush runs: the flush fails with 'shard … was deleted' and does not bring the index back. With manifest_retain_ms > 0, deleted indices stay restorable by a point-in-time branch until garbage collection expires them after the window.

Ops: every store start writes a tiny `search/wal/<node>/<n>.run` object; garbage collection keeps only the markers that are still needed. Manifest and state keys now use 20-digit epoch and generation fields, so the 16-digit keys of earlier dev builds are not read. The branch is unreleased, so no migration is needed.
